North Korea ordered the closure of Switzerland's diplomatic office in Pyongyang on 25 November and told its head to leave within 48 hours, over Swiss sanctions on a children's camp linked to deported Ukrainian children.
UKMTO reported three tankers struck in the Strait of Hormuz and a bulk carrier set on fire off Khor Fakkan on 22 November, bringing reported tanker strikes since 16 November to 10, gCaptain counts.
Iran's Revolutionary Guard said two tankers hit mines in Hormuz on 25 November; the claim names no ships and is unconfirmed. Iran also blacklisted 26 tugboats.
The IMO counts 25 seafarers confirmed dead in the Hormuz and wider Middle East shipping crisis as of 23 November; insurer The Swedish Club advises avoiding the strait.
Two Libyan soldiers died of injuries from the Ukrainian-claimed strike on Russian ships at Benghazi; France's foreign minister defended Ukraine's right to self-defence.
Russian strikes halted a Naftogaz gas site and cut power in five Ukrainian regions overnight into 25 November; the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant lost outside power again.
US negotiators have privately ruled out troops or bases in post-war Ukraine, the Kyiv Independent reports; Zelensky says 48 paid-for Patriot interceptors still await Pentagon sign-off.
